obtained.how: copy posted openly by REABIC (Regional Euro-Asian Biological Invasions Centre) in its publications folder: a re-typeset text with the original figures and Table 1 as images; Table 2 and the reference list are NOT included

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the copy's first page
bibliography.note: J. Great Lakes Res. 17(4): 425–436, 1991; Lin Wu and David A. Culver. Matches.

claims.claim: Daphnia clearance per animal F = 11.695·L^2.48 mL/d (11.7 at 1.0 mm, 32 at 1.5 mm), an allometry that reads 20–50 % above in-situ rates (Knoechel & Holtby 1986, via Wu & Culver 1991)
claims.source_value: Knoechel & Holtby's (1986) filtering rate–body length regression F = 11.695L^2.48 gives individual Daphnia filtering rates 20–50 % higher for western Lake Erie than Wu & Culver's own models; the authors attribute this to its pooling 'a broad range of cladoceran taxa'
claims.quote: Their model yields a 20-50% higher individual Daphnia filtering rate for the western basin
claims.conditions: comparison made with Wu & Culver's Daphnia size measurements from western Lake Erie; rates in mL ind⁻¹ d⁻¹, length in mm (head to base of spine)
claims.note: Arithmetic checked: 11.695 × 1.0^2.48 = 11.7; 11.695 × 1.5^2.48 = 11.695 × 2.733 = 32.0 mL/d. The regression is a multi-taxon cladoceran allometry, so the row's group would be better 'cladocerans (applied to Daphnia)'. The 20–50 % is relative to the authors' 32P in-situ models for the western basin, not to in-situ rates in general.

claims.claim: D. galeata mendotae in-situ clearance F = 3.837·L^1.343 mL/d; mean 4.3 at 0.95 mm; western Lake Erie, August
claims.note: The coefficients are in the article's Table 2, which the REABIC copy omits. The text confirms only that a significant western-basin regression of filtering rate (mL ind⁻¹ d⁻¹) on body length existed (F = 9.99, P < 0.0047; Fig. 2A, r = 0.57, N = 23), from 32P-yeast grazing chambers on 11–13 August 1987, and that its coefficients a and b were then applied to 1988–89 samples (p. 5). Fig. 2A's W line passes near 4 mL ind⁻¹ d⁻¹ at 1 mm, consistent with 3.837 at 1 mm, but a figure cannot confirm the digits.

tried.note: redirects to Elsevier linkinghub / ScienceDirect: subscription; the full article with Table 2 needs a library login

notes: The Table 2 claim (in-situ F = 3.837·L^1.343, mean 4.3 at 0.95 mm) stays unchecked until the human opens the ScienceDirect PDF. Other values in the copy: community grazing in August 1987 was roughly 130, 50 and 75 mL L⁻¹ d⁻¹ in the western, central and eastern basins (read from Fig. 1); large cladocerans did > 85 % of the grazing (Table 1); peak Daphnia grazing in 1988–89 was > 200 mL L⁻¹ d⁻¹ (the text: filtering the water every 1.2–7 days) and held edible algae below 5 mL m⁻³ (Figs 4–5). This REABIC copy is the one the research note (clear_water_phase_and_rotifers.md) links, and the note cites 'table 2' for the coefficients, but the copy has no Table 2: the note's coefficients were not read from this copy.
